newGame.hoodDifficultyGuide: The Hood: modular set difficulty guide
newGame.hoodDifficultyBands: The insert ranks this pack's sets from easiest (1) to hardest (9). For a lower-difficulty game, choose ranks 1–7; for moderate difficulty, 2–8; for higher difficulty, 3–9.

modularRules.mojo: You can swap the recommended modular sets for other genre sets. Longshot is optional and does not count toward the genre set total.
modularRules.core: Start with the modular set named on the main scheme. You may replace it with another set, chosen deliberately or at random. The core sets' difficulty ratings run from 1 to 5. Adding extra sets dilutes the encounter deck rather than necessarily making the scenario harder.
modularRules.gob: Each Green Goblin scenario calls for one modular encounter set and recommends Goblin Gimmicks. You may replace it with another set, chosen deliberately or at random. This pack also includes A Mess of Things, Power Drain, and Running Interference for customizing scenarios.
modularRules.twc: The Wrecking Crew uses its four villains' own encounter decks and does not use other encounter sets. Adjust its difficulty through the villain versions instead of adding modular sets.
modularRules.trors: Use the number of modular sets specified on the main scheme: three for Crossbones, two for Red Skull, and one for Absorbing Man, Taskmaster, or Zola. The named modular sets may be replaced when customizing the scenario. Taskmaster's required Hydra Patrol set and Crossbones' Experimental Weapons set are included automatically.
modularRules.toafk: Choose one modular encounter set. The insert recommends Temporal (difficulty 4) for a first game. For a harder game, replace it with Master of Time (difficulty 6) or Anachronauts (difficulty 8). These sets may also be used in other scenarios.
modularRules.gmw: Use the modular set listed for the scenario: Band of Badoon, Menagerie Medley, Space Pirates, or Kree Militants. You may replace that modular set when customizing the scenario. Other sets required by the scenario's setup remain included automatically.
modularRules.mts: Use the modular sets named on the main scheme: one for Tower Defense, or two for Ebony Maw, Thanos, Hela, or Loki. You may replace those modular sets when customizing the scenario. The Infinity Gauntlet remains required for Thanos and Loki and is included automatically.
modularRules.hood: Choose any seven modular encounter sets from this product or other products; you may choose them at random. No single lineup is specified. Set all seven aside, then shuffle one randomly chosen set into the encounter deck. The others are recruited during play.
modularRules.other: Follow the main scheme and product rulebook for the number of modular sets and any required encounter sets. Choose your own modular sets when no specific sets are recommended.
modularRules.mut_gen: Use the recommended modular sets: Brotherhood and Mystique for Sabretooth, Sentinels for Project Wideawake, Zero Tolerance for Master Mold, Mystique for Mansion Attack, and Acolytes for Magneto. You may replace these when customizing the scenario. Other required sets remain included automatically. Future Past uses a separate deck in campaign play.
modularRules.sm: Sinister Motives fixes certain modular sets to their scenarios: City in Chaos for Sandman, Symbiotic Strength for Venom and Venom Goblin, and Personal Nightmare for Mysterio. The other listed set may be replaced. Osborn Tech and Sinister Assault are added to campaign scenarios only when campaign rules direct it.
modularRules.next_evol: The recommended modular sets may be replaced. Keep each scenario’s required sets, including Hope Summers for Juggernaut, Mister Sinister and Stryfe. Campaign cards enter only when campaign instructions direct it.

version.title: Version
version.hint: Standard puts each villain's version A into play, expert its version B. Extreme starts each version A with its version B under it, entering play when it is defeated. Or the players choose version A or B for each villain.
